report:
PASS for the explicitly scoped sufficient-condition alternative: projective pullback trace data on scalar Hopf manifolds H_n, for every n≥3. The argument does not resolve unrestricted P18. Its substantive extensions are the all-dimensional BMP counterexample and extraction of every exceptional divisor over an arbitrary-dimensional projective base. The conclusions remain restricted to the stated ambient pullback data.

1. The higher-dimensional mass calculation is correct. Direct differentiation gives n−2 angular entries (μ+V_x)/μ and the displayed radial/fiber block. Its determinant is (1+V_{w bar w})Q[V]/(μ(1−μ)); the background block has determinant one. Thus the three positivity inequalities are dimension independent. Dividing the Xia–Zhang background and operator by 2π preserves the numerical potentials. Angular integration gives background density 2n(n−1)μ^(n−1)(1−μ), hence J_n=[n(n−1)/6](μ+V_x)^(n−3)J_3. These are independently verified calculations, not dimension analogy. The required original family and endpoint properties are present in [Xia–Zhang, Lemmas 2.1–2.3 and Proposition 4.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.21053v1).

On x<0, W has no x derivatives, so exact fiber integration removes F_{w bar w} and yields 12(μ+g′)[g″+μ(1−μ)]. Since 0<μ+g′≤μ and ∫|g″|≤2m, its integral is at most 3/2+24m. Consequently the threefold divergence occurs on x≥0, where μ+V_x≥1/4 for small η. The density identity then proves divergence in every n≥3. The endpoint descriptions give genuine smooth global potentials in all these dimensions. For any Hermitian h≥c(α+β), the potentials cV_η are admissible and their masses dominate c^n times this divergent mass. This establishes BMP failure for every Hermitian metric, without asserting anything about positive lower mass.

2. Divisorial extraction terminates as claimed. At each stage the auxiliary graph can be represented by the main component of a proper fiber product; it is compact and retains the original smooth neighborhood of generic D. Its divisor image is analytic. At a smooth generic center S of codimension c≥2, a least-order coordinate has pullback z_1^m times a unit, so the displayed coordinate ratios are holomorphic. The target blowup is smooth in that chart. The resolution theorem preserves this entire smooth locus, hence preserves the generic lift. The Jacobian identity gives J_new=J_old−(c−1)m, with J_new≥0. Therefore the process stops after finitely many steps, at a divisor image. These applications use [analytic blowups](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.01129), [proper mapping](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf), and [smooth-locus-preserving resolution](https://gokovagt.org/proceedings/2008/ggt08-wlodarczyk.pdf) with their hypotheses satisfied.

The terminal normal form (z_1,…,z_d,z′)↦(z_1^e,z_2,…,z_d) proves the ideal-order identity. For Lelong numbers, remove the generic divisorial logarithm. The residual has zero point Lelong number at very general points of F. Applying Skoda to every positive multiple, then Hölder with the ramification weight |y_1|^(2/e−2), proves exponential integrability of its pullback at every weight. A positive residual divisor coefficient would contradict this integrability when t times that coefficient is at least one. Thus the residual coefficient is zero, including when its restriction to F is identically −∞. The horizontal case follows from generic submersion coordinates. This checks both identities for every ideal and potential individually; no common finite selection of models is assumed.

3. The multiplier-ideal submersion proof is valid at every real weight. Fiber coefficient estimates put each Taylor coefficient in the base ideal. Finite Taylor truncations lie in its extended ideal, and Krull intersection supplies membership of the full germ. The other inclusion is Fubini. Restricting this identity gives the actual image ideal a_t=q* b_t. Local product coordinates also establish ν(p*U,Y)=0. Neither step uses the potentially undefined naive restriction U|B.

4. The closed-base exactness argument establishes its essential positive-mass antecedent. After choosing sufficient curvature room, the supplied restricted analytic models decrease to w. A common aκ/2-psh competitor z lies below w. Expanding its closed-background product gives mass(z in aκ)≥(a/2)^d; closed mass monotonicity transfers this lower bound to w, while comparison with zero gives mass(w)≤a^d. Thus the positive-mass model result applies. Together with preservation of each finite analytic singularity type, it gives ν(w,F)=lim_j 2^(−j)ord_F(b_(2^j))=τ_B(F). The relevant statements were checked in [Xia’s lecture manuscript](https://mingchenxia.github.io/Lectures/SGPT_final.pdf); the comparison is confined to the Kähler base, using [closed mass monotonicity](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.05796). Arbitrary decreasing quasi-psh convergence is not substituted for the model theorem.

For each divisor D on each Y-modification, extraction applied to q∘π gives the same factor e in the ideal and Lelong identities. Therefore the single potential q*w realizes all τ_Y(D) simultaneously. Horizontal divisors have both quantities zero. The quantifier over all modifications is retained throughout.

5. Full envelope descent is valid. The elliptic group preserves the background, the image ideals, and the entire constraint family. Its usc envelope is invariant and descends through local sections. For basic potentials, wedging with β and pushing forward proves equivalence of Ω_(a,b)-positivity and aκ-positivity on the base. Every base modification lifts to the smooth compact fiber product; the inverse image of its prime divisor is irreducible with generic multiplicity one. Hence the descended envelope satisfies every base constraint and is bounded above by w. The exact competitor gives the reverse inequality. In a larger arbitrary background Ω≥Ω_(a,b), the sandwich τ_Y(D)≤ν(T_Ω,D)≤ν(q*w,D)=τ_Y(D) proves exactness, without asserting descent or type independence there.

6. The mass and type conclusions have the correct scope. At bounded truncation level, horizontal degree and β²=0 give (Ω_(a,b)+dd^c q*v_j)^n=nb β∧q*(aκ+dd^c v_j)^d. Restricting to {v>−j} and taking the non-pluripolar limit yields the actual factor 2nb, since ∫_Eβ=2. This proves the stated positive finite individual mass and bounds. Only bounded local products from [BGL §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090) are needed; the BMP-dependent global unbounded-product theorem is not applied on H_n.

Equal base divisorial profiles identify ideals at every real weight; submersion pullback transfers this to the invariant Hopf backgrounds. Addition and positive homogeneity concern ideal classes, with backgrounds large enough to contain the summed or scaled potentials. They do not assert equality of normalized envelopes under addition. The full ordinary obstacle envelopes descend by the same invariance argument, with ordinary order equivalent by surjectivity. Their dyadic analytic models decrease to the trace. Pullback to each modification remains genuine and is bounded below by the limiting pullback; decreasing convergence therefore gives L¹ convergence there. Extraction also gives the claimed divisorial limits. No ordinary-type independence, extremal singularity-volume convergence, or capacity convergence is inferred.

7. The point example is correct, including the real-weight endpoints. In d normal variables, a term of degree k is integrable exactly when k>t−d, producing m_P^max(floor(t−d+1),0). Its asymptotic profile is ord_D(q*m_P). On the point blowup, the residual positive current has class aH−F and smooth semipositive representative (a−1)σ*κ+η. Mixed H/F intersections vanish, H^d=1 and F^d=(−1)^(d−1), so its top mass is a^d−1. The smooth product charges no exceptional divisor, giving the stated non-pluripolar mass 2nb(a^d−1). This example requires exceptional orders and is not merely exactness on one selected model.

The Hopf geometry and fiber normalization also check: H_n is diffeomorphic to S^(2n−1)×S¹, so b₁=1; it is non-Kähler. The form β has fiber mass two, Ω_(a,b) is Hermitian, and dΩ_(a,b)=−b dr∧α.

Harmless bibliographic correction: the live SGPT PDF retrieved for this audit is dated October 4, 2026, rather than July 18. The required statements are present in that retrieved version. Its nonstandard use of “modification” was checked against the appendix’s realization of arbitrary prime divisors. The private audit assertions, file hashes, prior readings, and requested reconstruction targets were not treated as mathematical evidence or granted assumptions.
